# Affine parameter directions realized by zero-face body cuts

This proves an actual tangent lemma at a FIXED limiting body and a finite-PL nonnegative parameter. An arbitrary signed affine parameter direction is realized by cutting away its negative part, with zero first-order body-volume cost. The logarithmic normalization has its ordinary derivative against dm/L, without a boundary-defect measure.

The final section gives an exact failure of uniformity along the truncated-triangle contact sequence. Thus this lemma does not remove a limiting tilted-volume defect from the selected-minimum argument without a further two-scale proof.

## 1. Setting and statement

Let P be a finite lattice-complete base and C its canonical positive-fiber hull. Write S for its sampled mixed set, dm for mixed volume, and M=m(S). Let

    L(w)=min_(1<=i<=q) A_i(w)

be a finite minimum of affine functions, nonnegative on C and strictly positive on every sampled fiber interior. Assume

    integral_S log L dm=0,    integral_S 1/L dm<infinity.         (1)

Boundary values of log L are interpreted almost everywhere; the boundary has zero mixed volume. Let h be ANY affine function on the full relative physical space, with either sign. For t>0 define

    C_t=C intersect {L+t h>=0}
       =C intersect all_i {A_i+t h>=0}.               (2)

For small t, all sampled fibers remain positive and compatible, and the base remains P. One can replace C_t by the canonical hull of its sampled fibers without changing any statement below. Set M_t=m(C_t intersect S). Then

    M−M_t=o(t),                                      (3)
    integral_(S outside C_t) |log L| dm=o(t),          (4)
    integral_(C_t intersect S) log(L+t h) dm
        =t integral_S h/L dm+o(t).                   (5)

The raw parameter in (5) can vanish on the new cut boundary. If strict positivity is desired, use

    U_t^raw=L+t h+t^2 on C_t,
    U_t=U_t^raw exp[−M_t^(−1) integral_(C_t intersect S)
                                             log U_t^raw dm].  (6)

It is strictly positive, continuous and concave on C_t. Put H=M^(−1) integral h/L. Uniformly on every compact own-interior mark set,

    U_t=L+t[h−L H]+o(t).                             (7)

The body path has bounded radial displacement O(t) and signed first boundary speed zero surface-almost everywhere in each sampled fiber. Thus its mass, covariance, every fixed closed-cap mass, and its energy at compact own-interior mark sets change by o(t). No smooth boundary or cap regularity is required for these zero-cost statements.

## 2. A geometric logarithmic tail lemma

Fix a sampled positive d-body K and an affine A>=0 on K. If A has a positive minimum there, all sufficiently small sublevel sets are empty. Suppose min_K A=0 and integral_K 1/A<infinity. Its continuous gradient is nonzero, because A cannot vanish identically on this positive fiber.

For d>=2 let g(s) be its coarea density:

    integral_K phi(A(X))dX=integral_0^B phi(s)g(s)ds.

The section-root g^(1/(d−1)) is concave on (0,B), with its one-sided endpoint value. Integrability of g(s)/s forces g(0)=0. Concavity and positivity at an interior level make g nondecreasing on some fixed interval (0,s_0). In detail, choose a later positive level, then a sufficiently small earlier level whose section root is smaller; concavity makes every secant still earlier positive.

For sufficiently small t with sqrt(t)<s_0,

    integral_t^(sqrt(t)) g(s)/s ds
        >=(1/2)g(t)|log t|.

The integral on the left tends to zero by integrability. Consequently

    g(t)|log t| ->0.                                 (8)

The same statement holds with t replaced by any fixed positive multiple of t. Monotonicity then gives

    m_K{A<=c t}<=c t g(c t)=o(t),
    integral_{A<=c t} |log A| dX
       <=g(c t) c t[1+|log(c t)|]=o(t).              (9)

In d=1, an affine function vanishing at an interval endpoint has divergent inverse integral. Thus under the present assumptions it has a positive minimum and the empty-sublevel case applies. This agrees with `candidate 9ae7c9f6778c4b49`.

For each A_i, integral 1/A_i<=integral 1/L<infinity. Partition the sampled set measurably according to the first index attaining L=min A_i. On the part assigned to i, L=A_i. Equations (9), summed over finitely many planes and fibers, therefore imply

    m{L<=c t}=o(t),
    integral_{L<=c t} |log L| dm=o(t).                (10)

This conclusion uses the actual affine-section geometry. Integrability of 1/L for an arbitrary measurable function alone would not justify inserting an unspecified quantitative logarithmic tail rate.

## 3. The retained collar after an affine tilt

We also need the new logarithm close to its NEW zero plane, where pointwise domination by |h|/L need not hold. The following estimate resolves it:

    integral_{X in K, 0<=A(X)<=c t, A(X)+t h(X)>0}
                       |log(A(X)+t h(X))| dX=o(t).   (11)

Here K,A are as in Section 2 and h is affine. Constants may depend on this fixed data.

Use fixed affine coordinates X=(q,s), s=A(X), with constant volume Jacobian. Choose a zero-face point as (0,0) and an interior point as (0,b), b>0; a shear supplies these coordinates. For H=2ct<b/2, let K_H be the q-section of K at height H. Projection of the cap 0<=s<=ct onto the q-space lies in 2 K_H. Indeed, for (q,s) in that cap, convexity puts

    ((b−H)/(b−s) q,H) in K.

The multiplier is between 1/2 and 1, and 0 belongs to K_H, so q lies in 2 K_H. The projection's (d−1)-volume is therefore at most a fixed constant times g(H).

Write h(q,s)=h_0+b_q.q+b_s s. The new scalar coordinate

    r=A+t h=(1+t b_s)s+t(h_0+b_q.q)

has ds/dr bounded above and below for small t. On the old collar 0<=A<=ct, boundedness of h gives 0<r<=C t whenever r is positive. Fubini in (q,r), using the projection bound, gives

    integral_collar |log r| dX
       <=C' g(2ct) integral_0^(Ct) |log r| dr
       <=C'' t(1+|log t|)g(2ct)=o(t)                 (12)

by (8). This proof handles a moving tilted plane, not only a parallel truncation.

For L=min A_i the active-index partition is unchanged after adding the SAME affine t h: on its i-th old piece, L+t h=A_i+t h. Dropping that piece restriction only increases the nonnegative bound in (11). Summing (11) therefore proves the corresponding retained-collar estimate for L.

## 4. Actual body compatibility and logarithmic differentiation

The set in (2) is convex: it is the intersection of C with finitely many affine halfspaces. For every sampled fiber choose an interior point o_z with L(z,o_z)>0. A sufficiently small inner homothety of K_z about o_z, of factor 1−C t, has L at least C t L(z,o_z), by concavity and nonnegativity of L. Choosing C using the bound for |h| puts that homothety inside C_t. Thus all sampled fibers remain positive, their Hausdorff and radial changes are O(t), and no old base disappears. Since the projection stays inside conv(P) and P is complete, no new integer base appears. Convexity gives exact anchored compatibility.

Choose H>=1+max_C |h|. Any removed point satisfies L<Ht. Equation (10) proves (3) and (4). At every old regular boundary point outside {L=0}, that point remains in C_t for all sufficiently small t, so its radial displacement is exactly zero eventually. Every zero affine face has zero (d−1)-area, since a positive-area zero face would make integral 1/A_i diverge. Hence the first inward boundary speed is zero almost everywhere. The O(t) radial bound supplies dominated convergence for the usual signed-shell formulas.

On the old bulk {L>2Ht}, no point is removed and

    |[log(L+t h)−log L]/t|<=2H/L.

Dominated convergence gives the integral limit integral h/L there as the collar shrinks. The missing tail of h/L tends to zero by integrability. On the old collar, (10) bounds the old absolute logarithm by o(t), and Section 3 bounds the retained new absolute logarithm by o(t). Adding these pieces proves (5).

All fixed closed-cap masses differ by at most the removed mass o(t), regardless of supporting statuses. Covariance and moments have bounded integrands and likewise change by o(t). The uniform energy shape envelope, applied to the bounded zero-speed radial path, gives E_(K_z(t))(y)=E_(K_z)(y)+o(t), uniformly near any compact set of old interior marks. This can also be seen directly by testing the old/new energy minimizers, whose kernels have a common positive floor and hence bound the energy change by a constant times removed volume.

## 5. A strictly positive floor costs only o(t)

On C_t every A_i+t h is nonnegative. Since

    log(1+eta/(L+t h))
        <=sum_i log(1+eta/(A_i+t h)),                 (13)

it suffices to estimate one affine denominator. If A_i has nonzero continuous gradient, the gradient of A_i+t h stays bounded away from zero for small t. The uniformly bounded section-area/coarea estimate gives

    integral_(K_z(t)) log(1+eta/(A_i+t h))
       <=C integral_0^B log(1+eta/s)ds
       =O(eta[1+|log eta|]).                         (14)

If its continuous gradient is zero, its value at each old sampled fiber is a fixed positive number; positivity of L on fiber interiors rules out zero. It consequently remains uniformly positive on those fibers for small t, and the integral is O(eta). There are only finitely many planes and fibers. Choosing eta=t^2 in (13)–(14) changes the logarithmic integral by o(t).

Equations (3), (5) and the old mean-log normalization now give

    M_t^(−1) integral_(S_t) log(L+t h+t^2)dm
       =t H+o(t),  H=M^(−1)integral_S h/L dm.

This proves (6)–(7). It is a genuine positive-parameter path, not merely a formal direction in a cone with ignored zero constraints.

## 6. Exact noncommutation with the boundary-atom sequence

The construction in `candidate 1b1d5e313c1943d1` has

    K_m={x,y>=0, 1/m<=x+y<=1},
    L_m=c_m[x+y−1/m+2^(−m)],
    c_m ->c=exp(1/2),  V_m ->1/2,
    integral_(K_m) 1/(L_m/c_m) ->1+log 2.

At every fixed m, for h=−1 and sufficiently small t the body cut is empty, because min L_m>0. Thus its mean-log derivative is exactly

    −(1/V_m)integral_(K_m) 1/L_m
       ->−2 exp(−1/2)(1+log 2).                     (15)

At the limiting triangle K={x,y>=0,x+y<=1}, L=c(x+y). The coupled cut is {x+y>=t/c}, with removed volume t^2/(2c^2). Its exact retained raw logarithmic integral is

    I(t)=c^(−2){(c−t)^2 log(c−t)/2−(c−t)^2/4
                    +t[(c−t)log(c−t)−(c−t)]}.

Since log c=1/2, I(0)=0 and I'(0)=−1/c. Dividing by the limiting volume gives the derivative

    −2 exp(−1/2),                                    (16)

as required by (5). The difference between (15) and (16) is precisely the mass 2 exp(−1/2)log 2 of the tilted-volume boundary defect. Adding the t^2 positivity floor changes neither derivative.

Therefore differentiation before the moving-body limit and differentiation at the limit do not commute, even for this one-plane, one-source contact sequence with uniform source cores. The first-order o(t) estimates in the present theorem are for a FIXED limiting pair. They cannot be treated as uniform in a selected epsilon sequence without a separate quantitative choice of the cutting scale relative to that sequence.

No claim here excludes defects at actual joint minima. The theorem instead supplies a precise actual coupled tangent and an exact calibration of the missing limit-exchange issue.
